source: BBOC 2025 MAC Betting Preview (Mike Calabrese/Josh 'Duck' Nunn/Stuckey)

teams.key_avoids: 2nd-easiest schedule; faces 10 new QBs (2nd-most). Opens Kentucky (revenge) + Western Kentucky; unusual conf road trip to Washington State; the futures-defining game is at Miami-OH in wk12; closes Ball State + Central Michigan.
teams.bboc_notes: Pick to reach Detroit — the most talented MAC roster as usual, Stuckey ~8.5 (6.25 projected league wins, most in the league), Mike leans over, Duck bullish. Bake in the Jason Candle letdown: he's lost 24 games as a favorite since 2016 (2nd-most in FBS), so 'once a year' he drops one he shouldn't. Gleason is the Rorschach test — the only G5 QB back with 3,000 yds/30 TD/≤13 TO, but dreadful under pressure and prone to bonehead games (Buffalo, Bowling Green, Ohio). OL more experienced (0→45 returning starts); RB room upgraded (Chip Trayanum, Kanye Christian) to finally get a run game; Vandagriff/Vander Oss + Trayvon Rudolph give elite weapons. DL always deep but LBs are a concern and run defense may be the weakness. Mike likes over 8.5 and a 20-1 CFP flyer.

teams.key_avoids: Brutal non-con (Merrimack opener not assured, at Texas Tech, Buffalo, at FSU, at OU). Duck has them >28.5-pt dogs at least five times. Winnable: UMass home, at Ball State, at Akron, Central Michigan home — but all suspect.
teams.bboc_notes: Universally the worst team in the MAC — lost 21 straight, went winless in 2024 (incl. an FCS loss), worst run defense in the MAC in a decade (5.9 YPC, 36 rush TD allowed). HC fired for cause in the offseason (credit-card/conflict-of-interest violations) six weeks before camp; the DC also bailed to be a position coach. Roster gutted by the portal (Stephen Daley, McCrae, Cam Olds all gone). Stuckey projects 1.8 and shows a little value on the under but PASSES (over 1.5 is ~-180, implied ~2.1). Duck went under 1.5 CONFERENCE wins and would need +59.5 to back them in a non-con road game. 'Not an FBS roster.'

teams.qb_status: Transfer — DeQuan Finn (returns to MAC from Baylor)
teams.key_avoids: Bookended by tough games — at Wisconsin, at Rutgers, UNLV early, then at Ohio, host Toledo, at Buffalo in a 15-day window late. Does NOT get Kent or UMass. Could start 0-3 (UNLV shuffled to after a bye).
teams.bboc_notes: Everywhere you turn it's 'yeah, but' — returns ZERO offensive starters, 128th-130th in returning production, lost the top-13 snap counts up front (6 to NFL/P4) plus a 6-year starting QB. DeQuan Finn (back from Baylor) is a mobile boom/bust passer (three 94+ QBR MAC starts and three ≤35 QBR starts at Toledo) whose legs may be needed behind a rebuilt line. Lost All-MAC LBs Matt Salopek + Wise and DE Ugu; strength is the safeties (though best corner Straiter left for Auburn). Chuck Martin/Bill Brechin mail in non-con vanilla to stay healthy. Mike leans over, Stuckey passes (~6.3-6.45). HOST SPLIT; Duck says don't bet the MAC future now — wait until they're 0-3 for ~1000-1 value.

teams.key_avoids: Significant road dogs at Wyoming, Nebraska, UAB; at Toledo, host Central Michigan in conf. Winnable: UMass + Kent home late (motivation?), at Ball State, at BG. INELIGIBLE for the postseason (APR) — and no real bye (first bye Nov 1, last week bye is meaningless).
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT — Stuckey projects ~4.8 and shows value on the over (over 4 -120) but hasn't pulled the trigger over the mental-checkout risk; Duck went UNDER 4.5. The APR situation is scary: postseason-ineligible with a practice reduction and a Level-1 penalty, with writers noting a path to losing FBS standing. Ben Finley provides real experience (9:2 TD:INT close to 2024); but the defense lost its top-9 snap counts (CJ Nunnally, Brian McCoy to Okla St), the chronic OL problem means no run game, and they lost an insane punter + kicker (special teams could plummet). Where are they mentally with nothing to play for?

teams.key_avoids: Won the MAC schedule lottery — significant favorite in the first six MAC games, a very realistic 6-0 start. It comes down to hosting Miami-OH and Ohio (the two swing games). Wk1 at Minnesota (Duck bet Buffalo).
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT — Duck's pick to WIN the MAC (bet it at 8-1) on personnel + coaching (Pete Lembo) + the schedule; Stuckey PASSES, thinks they've been over-bet all summer. Returns the 9th-most defensive production in the nation — 12 of the top-14 tacklers back, incl. Red Murdock (2nd in FBS in tackles behind the departed Shaun Dolac) — plus stars Kobe Stewart (9.5 sacks), Deion Crawford (8.5). Ta'Quan Roberson mirrors CJ Agbana's dual-threat profile with better WRs. Cautions: bottom-5 portal class, and 2024's eight wins were mostly close/out-gained games (high floor, not high ceiling). OL (RT/center) + WR depth questions.

teams.qb_status: Battle — Grant Jordan (Yale, likely) / Brandon Rose (Utah) / AJ Hairston
teams.key_avoids: Rejoins the MAC. Big game is Temple at home wk1. Duck bet the wk1 UNDER (52.5) expecting run-heavy, slow tempo. 7-8 winnable games on a soft slate but bottom-10 in returning production.
teams.bboc_notes: New HC Joe Harasymiak (built Maine into an FCS winner) with a Rutgers-assistant DC and ex-Northwestern OC Mike Pajakian — expect a run-first, slow, ball-control team. Bottom-10 nationally in returning production; lost the top-7 rushers (Hesters to Michigan, etc.) and top WR Kay'Ron Lynch-James (Lions), with only ~20 career FBS OL starts on the roster. Both hosts like Grant Jordan (Yale, mobile, late bloomer) as the QB to win the job — the one variable that changes how they'd bet UMass. Stuckey projects ~4 but passes on the uncertainty; Duck fades the run-heavy scheme in totals. New kicker/punter from the P4.

teams.key_avoids: Faces 11 new starting QBs — the most in FBS (highest-variance schedule). Likely 1-3 start; the West Virginia home game is the trap (Rich Rod revenge). Hosts Toledo + Miami-OH; small dog at Buffalo.
teams.bboc_notes: BIG HOST SPLIT — Mike is OVER 7.5 and took Ohio to win the MAC at 7/2 (retained the family: new HC Brian Smith promoted internally, DC John Hauser kept, plundered secondary refilled from Wisconsin/UK/Ohio St/Minnesota); Stuckey's FAVORITE UNDER of the conference (projects 6.5, promises to drive to Athens in Ohio gear if wrong again after whiffing on them last year); Duck leans under, wait-and-see. Parker Navarro returns (1,000 non-sack rush yds) but 17 TWP to 14 BTT. The DL that carried them was gutted (Weaver→Rutgers, others to Missouri/Maryland), all LBs lost — the secondary is the lone strength. Developmental year; run D could get eaten early.

teams.key_avoids: Winnable: Kent, Akron at home, at Western Michigan, Eastern Michigan — that stretch probably decides the total. Duck fades wk1 at Purdue and vs UConn. Ohio at home.
teams.bboc_notes: Year-zero rebuild — new HC Mike Uremovich (also the OC, ex-Butler, ex-NIU assistant) brings a pistol/12-personnel run scheme that may fit run-first QB Kyle Kelly, but Kelly must prove he can throw (53% comp, 4.7 YPA in 2023 before moving to corner). 126th in returning production, 134th on offense; lost 8 of the top-10 offensive snap counts (mostly to P4) + four multi-year OL starters. The secondary was atrocious (eleven 50+ yд plays, 37 pass TD allowed, 5.2 YPC) and the front seven is massively undersized; portal backfill is fringe FCS. Duck fades them throughout; Stuckey projects 3.6 and passes.

teams.key_avoids: Final MAC season (off to the Mountain West). Non-con at Maryland, Mississippi State, hosts San Diego State. Draws Toledo + Miami-OH (two of those three on the road). Floor games: Holy Cross, Ball State, Kent at home.
teams.bboc_notes: All three effectively UNDER (Stuckey projects 6.0, lean under; Mike + Duck under 6.5) — no host split. 136th in returning production (DEAD LAST). The defense that beat Notre Dame was gutted — DL (Haberman to Titans, Gill-Howard to Texas Tech), all LBs, and an underrated secondary all gone to NFL/P4, and DC Nick Benedetto left for Fresno State. New OC Quinn Sanders (from D2 Charleston, WV) installs a run-centric attack behind a line replacing four starters; new DC Rob Harley's Arkansas State units were 127th/129th in total D. Stuckey: the faster spread they want to run 'doesn't fit who NIU should be.' A look-ahead-to-next-year year.

teams.qb_status: Battle — Noah Kim / Cameron Edge / Jace Stuckey / Salem
teams.key_avoids: Toughest MAC slate late; AVOIDS Kent, Akron AND Toledo; no bye until November (two late byes, which may hurt a late-peaking Creighton team). A lot rides on the four reset opponents (CMU, Ball State, NIU, Bowling Green).
teams.bboc_notes: All three PASS — 'never go under on Eastern Michigan.' Chris Creighton is one of the most underrated coaches in the country: doesn't beat himself, good special teams, low penalties, and 73 of the last 97 games have been one-possession. Both coordinators return for a third straight year. But the roster lost a ton — top-4 DL, top-2 LBs, top-3 DBs, plus the QB/RB/top-2 WRs on offense — so there's a real four-way QB battle (cousin Jace Stuckey is ~4th; Kim/Edge have upside). Stuckey projects ~4 near market. High variance because the four reset opponents swing the total. Don't fade Creighton this low.

teams.qb_status: Battle — Joe Labas / Angel Flores (NAU) / Marcus Beam (JUCO)
teams.key_avoids: Brutal open — at San Jose State, at Pitt, at Michigan (probable 0-3). AVOIDS Ohio, Miami-OH, NIU and Ball State; gets Toledo AND Buffalo at home late (the move-making window). Winnable early: Wagner, Akron, Kent, UMass.
teams.bboc_notes: THE REGRESSION/DARK-HORSE team — all three take the future (Mike + Stuckey; Stuckey's bold call is CMU upsetting Toledo in the MAC title game), though none bets the win total over (too much variance/depth risk). CMU was -42 in turnover margin over three years and lost its top-5 WRs to injury in 2024 — 'if any team gets every bounce, it's this one.' New staff all first-time in their FBS roles: HC Matt Drinkall (Army roots, wants to run), OC Jim Chapin (Eastern Washington, top-10 FCS offense), DC Sean Cronin (Army DL, elite red-zone D). Power-spread with 12/13-personnel + varied tempo; QB battle (Labas the likely runner). Fire up chips — flyer at 22-1 (shop to ~12-1).

teams.key_avoids: Tough non-con (Cincinnati, Louisville, Liberty → likely 1-3). Bye before Toledo (Stuckey's angle — Toledo's run D may be soft). Plays the top three AND bottom three; late road at EMU, Kent, UMass.
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT of degree — Duck bet UNDER 6.5 early (ceiling 6-6, likely 5-7); Stuckey leans under (~6.0) but likes a little 20-1 future flyer on the George hire + violent run identity in a MAC full of weak front sevens. New HC Eddie George (from Tennessee State, hired late March 9) with new coordinators. 127th-130th in returning production; the defense that carried them is a FULL rebuild (0 returning starters, 13 of top-15 tacklers gone), and they lost do-everything TE Harold Fannin + RB Terion Stewart. Power 12/13-personnel run scheme; big drop-off from QB1 Drew Pine to QB2. Fade vs P4; the last-game UMass spot could be treacherous if not bowl-motivated.

teams.key_avoids: Likely 0-4 start (at Michigan State, North Texas, at Illinois, then FCS). Does NOT get Kent or Akron; HOSTS Ohio + Toledo. Road league games (UMass, EMU, at Miami) not awful.
teams.bboc_notes: A pass for all three (Mike leans under; Stuckey close to market, projects ~+2; Duck no strong opinion). ZERO returning OL starters (lost four good ones, two now on the Dolphins), 132nd on offense — the domino that threatens everything. QB is murky (Brady Jones vs Brock Lowry, only ~9 career FBS pass attempts between the room). RB Jalen Buckley is a legit MAC back but has no Nixon-type complement (UCF) and could be stacked against. Defense lost the top-3 LBs, gutted DL (11 of 13 sacks gone), and bled spring-portal pieces (Jefferson→Louisville, Nelson/Green to Vandy/Memphis); good size on the line + CB Jordan Thomas the hopes. Going after P4 cast-offs — if they hit, maybe something; if not, a cliff.
